HTTP method semantics are not business-effect deduplication [RFC 9110, §9.2.1–9.2.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-9.2.2) defines the semantics of safe and idempotent methods. A safe method is intended not to request a state-changing effect. Idempotency describes the intended server-side effect of repeating an identical request; it does not require the responses, timing or logging events to be identical. PUT, DELETE and safe methods are idempotent by their specified semantics. POST has no general automatic-retry guarantee. Three distinct notions must not be merged: 1. **HTTP method contract:** Is the requested operation safe or idempotent according to its semantic

If every carrier is occupied by pinned waiters, the signaled thread cannot make progress even when the lock itself has been released. An observer may then see a live process, an apparently free lock and no completed requests. That is a scheduler/resource interlock, not necessarily a permanently held mutex. items.excerpt: ## A stopping rule A practical stopping rule is: 1. Run a pilot with at least 10 replications. 2. Estimate the standard error of the primary metric. 3. Compute the required n for the target relative error. 4. Run to that n or to a declared budget, whichever is smaller. 5. Record the achieved error and whether the target was met. V12 does not adapt n during a run. The scenario declares the replication count, and the run reports the achieved error. This keeps the result reproducible; an adaptive stopping rule would need its own seeded decision log.

The sensitivity run reports a quadratic response-surface screen and is converged. A separate two-replication convergence-stress run is marked insufficient-sample. items.excerpt: ## The Monte Carlo procedure 1. State the model and the output metric. 2. Declare a distribution or range for each uncertain input, with its evidence status. 3. Declare correlations between inputs, or state that they are independent. 4. Generate a sample matrix with a recorded seed. 5. Run the model for each row and each replication. 6. Report the output mean, standard error and confidence interval. 7. Decompose the output variance into main and interaction terms. 8. Record the assumptions, the sample size and the limits. The V12 engine implements steps 4-7. The scenario contract records steps 1-3; the run record records steps 4-8.

items.excerpt: ## Evidence and limits The source ledger records the exact unit, representation hash, sections read, omissions and limits for each admitted source. The engine tests exercise conservation, boundary cases, event ordering, retries, convergence and sensitivity ranking. Those tests prove the implemented reference cases; they do not validate a real system. All numeric workloads in this volume are synthetic. The confidence intervals use a normal approximation across replications. The sensitivity screen uses a quadratic response-surface decomposition, not a full pick-freeze Sobol analysis. Calibration is `uncalibrated` for every model. Independent review and owner acceptance remain separate decision

items.excerpt: ## V12-E: decision validity The decision records declare: - candidates and their runs; - hard, soft and non-quantitative constraints; - business-comparable metrics with units; - evidence statuses for model verification, calibration and simulation; - an explicit recommendation or a no-recommendation outcome; - non-quantitative constraints kept separate; - reversal triggers and limitations. The checkout record is decision-supported under its declared constraints. The modernization record is insufficient evidence. Both are valid outcomes.
